overview.description: Siberian Huskies are medium-sized working dogs bred by the Chukchi people of northeastern Asia. They possess a unique metabolism evolved for endurance and cold climates, requiring specific dietary considerations.
common_health_sensitivities: Food allergies / sensitivities (often to specific grains or proteins)

puppy.notes: High energy density required for rapid bone and muscle development without excessive growth spurts.

adult_working.notes: Designed for endurance sledding; high fat is crucial for sustained energy release.

adult_pet.notes: Standard maintenance diet for companion Huskies with moderate daily exercise.

senior.notes: Easily digestible proteins, joint supplements (glucosamine/chondroitin), and lower calories to prevent weight gain.

key_nutrients.importance: Critical for Siberian Huskies due to genetic predisposition to poor zinc absorption, leading to skin lesions and coat issues.
key_nutrients.recommended_sources: Red meat, poultry, zinc proteinate supplements.

key_nutrients.importance: Supports double coat health, reduces skin inflammation, and aids cognitive function.
key_nutrients.recommended_sources: Salmon oil, krill oil, wild-caught fish.

key_nutrients.importance: Maintains lean muscle mass and supports high metabolic output.
key_nutrients.recommended_sources: Chicken, turkey, lamb, beef, fish, eggs.

meats_and_proteins.name: Chicken (Cooked, Plain)
meats_and_proteins.benefit: Lean source of essential amino acids.
meats_and_proteins.preparation: Boiled or baked without seasoning, bones removed.

meats_and_proteins.name: Beef (Lean)
meats_and_proteins.benefit: Excellent source of iron, zinc, and B vitamins.

meats_and_proteins.name: Salmon (Cooked)
meats_and_proteins.benefit: Rich in Omega-3 fatty acids for coat and skin.

meats_and_proteins.name: Eggs (Cooked)
meats_and_proteins.benefit: Complete protein and biotin for coat sheen.

vegetables.name: Carrots
vegetables.benefit: Low-calorie crunch, great for dental health and beta-carotene.
vegetables.preparation: Raw or steamed, cut into bite-sized pieces.

vegetables.name: Green Beans
vegetables.benefit: High fiber, vitamins A, C, and K; good for weight management.
vegetables.preparation: Fresh or plain frozen, steamed or raw.

vegetables.name: Pumpkin (Plain Canned)
vegetables.benefit: Excellent for digestive health and firming stools.
vegetables.preparation: Plain 100% pure pumpkin puree (no pie filling).

vegetables.name: Sweet Potatoes
vegetables.preparation: Cooked, peeled, and mashed or cubed.

vegetables.name: Broccoli
vegetables.benefit: Rich in fiber and Vitamin C (feed in moderation).

fruits.name: Apples
fruits.benefit: Vitamins A and C, dietary fiber (remove seeds and core).
fruits.preparation: Sliced, core and seeds completely removed.

fruits.name: Watermelon
fruits.benefit: Hydrating, rich in vitamins A, B6, and C (seedless/rindless).

fruits.name: Bananas
fruits.benefit: Potassium, vitamins, and biotin (feed in moderation due to sugar).

grains_and_carbs.name: Rice (White or Brown)
grains_and_carbs.benefit: Easily digestible energy source, especially soothing for upset stomachs.

grains_and_carbs.name: Oatmeal
grains_and_carbs.benefit: Soluble fiber, good for dogs with wheat sensitivities.

grains_and_carbs.name: Quinoa
grains_and_carbs.benefit: Complete plant-based protein and mineral source.

toxic_foods.symptoms: Vomiting, diarrhea, increased heart rate, seizures, death.

toxic_foods.toxic_agent: Unknown toxin causing sudden kidney failure
toxic_foods.symptoms: Lethargy, vomiting, diarrhea, lack of appetite, oliguria.
Oxidative damage to red blood cells, hemolytic anemia, weakness, pale gums.

toxic_foods.toxic_agent: Massive insulin release causing acute hypoglycemia and liver failure
toxic_foods.symptoms: Vomiting, lethargy, loss of coordination, seizures, liver failure within hours.
Severe central nervous system depression, respiratory failure, coma, death.

toxic_foods.toxic_agent: Persin (found in fruit, pit, leaves, and bark)
toxic_foods.symptoms: Vomiting, diarrhea, myocardial congestion (especially toxic to birds/horses, mild in dogs).
Restlessness, rapid breathing, heart palpitations, muscle tremors, seizures.
Internal lacerations, choking, gastrointestinal perforation, bowel obstruction.

toxic_foods.toxic_agent: Ethanol production and gas expansion in stomach
toxic_foods.symptoms: Severe abdominal distension, gastric torsion (bloat), alcohol poisoning.

frequency.puppies: 3 to 4 meals per day until 6 months, then 2 meals daily.
frequency.adults: 2 meals per day to prevent gastric torsion (bloat) and maintain steady energy.

feeding_guidelines.hydration: Always provide fresh, clean water. Huskies, coming from arctic climates, particularly appreciate cool, clean water and need ample hydration especially during warmer months.
tips: Avoid rigorous exercise 1 hour before and after meals to minimize risk of bloat (GDV).
Monitor coat condition regularly; dull coats or dry skin may indicate zinc deficiency or fatty acid imbalance.
Adjust portion sizes based on activity level—working/sledding Huskies require significantly higher caloric intake than sedentary house pets.
